newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Search intensifies for missing yacht off Australia.
newsitem.headline: Search intensifies for missing yacht off Australia.

text.p: Australian rescue officials said on Thursday they were intensifying a search for five people after debris and lifejackets from their missing yacht were found off Australia's north-east coast.
Four men and an 18-year-old woman were aboard the yacht. Three of the men were from New Zealand while the woman and a fourth man were Australian.

Australian defence force spokesman Brigadier Paul Tys told reporters the Australian navy frigate HMAS Melbourne was expected to arrive early on Friday in the search area in the Coral Sea about 500 km (300 miles) south-west of the Solomon Islands capital of Honiara.
Tys said three lifejackets from the 14-metre New Zealand-registered schooner Queen Charlotte were picked up on Thursday by a merchant ship in the area.
The yacht released a series of distress signals after sailing into heavy weather from Tropical Cyclone Justin, which has been hovering off the Australian coast for two weeks.
The lifejackets found were for use in light, coastal conditions and were among 12 on board.
"There's a ray of hope in that there were 12 lifejackets," said Tys, who added the crew were likely to be wearing jackets more suited to heavy conditions.
A distress beacon bearing the name Queen Charlotte was also found near the lifejackets, Tys said.

Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Gray said it was possible the five people had taken to a liferaft, with the search concentrated on an area 60 km west of where the lifejackets and debris were found.
"We're still hopeful that we're going to find a liferaft," Gray said.
